_note: Batch D: discovery candidates drafted by Claude from clusters of real NTSB reports inside each CICTT parent (tools/discover_clusters.py: k-means on report vectors, class TF-IDF terms, most common coded findings). Drafts for SME review, not approved categories. They target general-aviation patterns the 37 package candidates (transport-oriented) do not cover.

candidates.name: Carburetor icing leading to loss of engine power
candidates.definition: Ice forms in the carburetor in conditions conducive to carburetor icing, often at reduced power, and the engine loses partial or total power because carburetor heat was not applied or was applied too late.

candidates.name: Fuel exhaustion from inadequate fuel planning
candidates.definition: The engine stops because all usable fuel on board was used up: the pilot did not plan enough fuel for the flight, did not verify the quantity before departure, or continued past the point where a fuel stop was needed.

candidates.name: Fuel starvation from fuel selector or tank mismanagement
candidates.definition: Fuel remains on board but does not reach the engine because the pilot selected an empty tank, positioned the fuel selector incorrectly, or did not switch tanks, and the engine loses power.

candidates.name: Loss of directional control in a crosswind on landing
candidates.definition: During the landing roll in a crosswind or gusting wind the pilot does not maintain directional control and the airplane veers off the runway, ground loops or strikes objects beside the runway.

candidates.name: Ground loop in a tailwheel airplane
candidates.definition: A tailwheel (conventional gear) airplane swerves and ground loops during takeoff or landing because the pilot does not maintain directional control with rudder and brakes.

candidates.name: Bounced landing and improper recovery
candidates.definition: The airplane touches down hard or at the wrong pitch attitude, bounces, and the pilot's recovery from the bounce or improper flare leads to a hard landing, porpoising, or damage to the nose gear, firewall or propeller.

candidates.name: Gear-up landing with the landing gear not extended
candidates.definition: The pilot lands a retractable-gear airplane with the landing gear retracted because gear extension was forgotten, the before-landing checklist was not completed, or the gear warning was missed.

candidates.name: Aerodynamic stall in the traffic pattern or on approach
candidates.definition: While maneuvering at low altitude in the traffic pattern, on the turn to final or on approach, the pilot lets the airspeed decay or the angle of attack exceed the critical value, and the airplane stalls and loses height before recovery is possible.

candidates.name: Stall after takeoff at high density altitude
candidates.definition: The airplane cannot climb as expected after takeoff because of high density altitude, heavy weight or a short or rising field, and the pilot pulls the nose up until the airplane stalls or settles into terrain.

candidates.name: Wire strike during low-altitude flight
candidates.definition: During low-altitude flight, such as agricultural application, maneuvering or a low pass, the aircraft collides with power lines or other wires the pilot did not see or did not keep clear of.

candidates.name: Spatial disorientation after VFR flight into instrument conditions
candidates.definition: A pilot flying under visual flight rules continues into clouds, darkness or low visibility, becomes spatially disoriented, and loses control of the aircraft or flies into terrain.

candidates.name: Reciprocating engine failure from a connecting rod or crankshaft fracture
candidates.definition: A piston engine fails in flight because a connecting rod, rod bearing, crankshaft or cylinder fractures, often after oil starvation or a maintenance error, and the engine loses all power.

candidates.name: Loss of tail rotor effectiveness in a helicopter
candidates.definition: A helicopter experiences an uncommanded yaw, such as loss of tail rotor effectiveness in a crosswind or tailwind at low airspeed, or a tail rotor drive failure, and the pilot cannot regain yaw control.

candidates.name: Low rotor RPM in a helicopter
candidates.definition: The helicopter's main rotor speed decays below the normal range because of high power demand, a mishandled throttle or collective, or a late autorotation entry, and the helicopter descends uncontrollably.

candidates.name: Balloon hard landing in high wind
candidates.definition: A hot-air balloon lands in strong or gusty surface wind, the basket strikes the ground hard, tips or is dragged, and occupants are injured.

candidates.name: Taxi collision from inadequate visual lookout
candidates.definition: While taxiing, the pilot does not maintain an adequate visual lookout and the aircraft strikes another aircraft, a vehicle, a hangar or another object on the ramp or taxiway.
